hook.situation: You tried a new restaurant, class, cafe, or event and want to tell a friend what you noticed. The point is not just that something happened, but that you personally saw the result or watched it change.
objectives: Use 가 보니까 and -더라고요 to report firsthand observations.
Use -더니 to connect an observed earlier state to a later change.
Keep -더니 separate from -았/었더니, which is used for your own action leading to a result.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean often marks the source of your information. -더라고요 tells the listener, 'I noticed this myself,' while -더니 tells a small before-and-after story that you watched unfold.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-더라고요 — what I noticed firsthand
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use -더라고요 when you are reporting an earlier observation from your own eyes, ears, feelings, or experience.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -더라고요 to a verb or adjective stem: 많더라고요, 조용하더라고요, 빨리 나오더라고요. In casual speech, -더라 is common.

examples.ko: 그 식당에 가 보니까 생각보다 조용하더라고요.
examples.romanization: geu sikdange ga bonikka saenggakboda joyonghadeoragoyo.
examples.en: When I tried going to that restaurant, it was quieter than I expected.
examples.note: The speaker went there and noticed it.

examples.en: The food came out faster than I expected.
After listening myself, I noticed the explanation was easy.
examples.note: Useful for class, lecture, or tutorial reviews.

exceptions: Do not use -더라고요 for pure hearsay. If you only heard it from someone else, use reported speech.
Avoid using it for your own planned action as if you observed yourself from outside.
Plain past -았/었어요 states a fact. -더라고요 adds your firsthand noticing.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-더니 — I watched X, and then Y changed
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -더니 is a before-and-after connector with eyewitness flavor. The first part is what you observed; the second part is the change or result.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -더니 to a verb or adjective stem: 조용하더니, 기침하더니, 오더니. For your own action causing a result, use -았/었더니: 많이 먹었더니 졸렸어요.

examples.en: It was quiet at first, and then it quickly got crowded, I noticed.
It was raining in the morning, and then it cleared up in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 친구가 계속 기침하더니 결국 감기에 걸렸어요.
examples.romanization: chinguga gyesok gichimhadeoni gyeolguk gamgie geollyeosseoyo.
examples.en: My friend kept coughing, and then ended up catching a cold.
examples.note: Observed repeated action followed by result.

examples.en: I ate a lot, so I got sleepy.
examples.note: This is -았/었더니 for my own action, not plain -더니.

exceptions: Plain -더니 usually does not narrate your own neutral action: 내가 가더니 sounds strange in most learner sentences.
Use -니까 for a simple logical reason when firsthand change is not important.
Use -는데 when you only need background, not a watched change.

exampleSentence.en: When I tried going, it was better than I expected.
exampleSentence.note: Experience leads into a firsthand observation.

exampleSentence.en: There were more people than I expected, I noticed.
exampleSentence.note: Reports what the speaker personally saw.

extendedVocabulary.english: I observed X, and then Y happened

exampleSentence.en: It was quiet at first, and then it quickly got crowded, I noticed.
The food came out faster than expected, I noticed.
It was quiet at first, and then there were quickly more people.
exampleSentence.note: Sets the first stage before a change.

exampleSentence.en: I heard there used to be fewer people.
These days, the atmosphere has changed a lot, I noticed.
When it became lunchtime, the restaurant got crowded, I noticed.
At first, the restaurant was quiet, I noticed.
It was quiet at first, and then there were quickly more people.
These days, the atmosphere has changed a lot, I noticed.
These days, the number of people has increased a lot, I noticed.
These days, the waiting time has decreased, I noticed.
exampleSentence.note: Opposite of 늘다 for observed change.

extendedVocabulary.english: to come to know; to find out

exampleSentence.ko: 직접 가 보니까 왜 유명한지 알게 됐어요.
exampleSentence.en: After going there myself, I found out why it is famous.

exampleSentence.ko: 일주일 동안 분위기가 어떻게 변하는지 관찰했어요.
exampleSentence.en: I observed how the atmosphere changed over a week.

extendedDialogue.setting: A friend asks about a new restaurant after someone visited it.

lines.grammarNote: 가 보니까 asks for a report based on actual experience.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: It came out faster than expected, and the taste was good too.
lines.grammarNote: 생각보다 plus -더라고요 compares expectation with firsthand experience.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Right. These days, the atmosphere has changed a lot, I noticed.
lines.grammarNote: 요즘은 and -더라고요 report the current state the speaker noticed.

readingText.title: 가 보니까 생각보다 괜찮더라고요
readingText.body: 새 식당이나 카페에 다녀온 뒤에는 그냥 '좋았어요'라고 말할 수도 있지만, 직접 보고 느낀 느낌을 살리려면 '-더라고요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '가 보니까 생각보다 조용하더라고요'라고 하면 내가 직접 가서 알게 된 정보라는 느낌이 들어요. 시간이 지나면서 변한 모습을 말할 때는 '-더니'가 좋아요. 예를 들어 '처음에는 조용하더니 금방 붐비더라고요'라고 하면 처음 상태와 나중 상태가 한 장면처럼 이어져요. 하지만 내 행동 때문에 생긴 결과라면 '많이 먹었더니 졸렸어요'처럼 '-았/었더니'를 써야 해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: After visiting a restaurant or cafe, -더라고요 lets you report what you personally noticed. -더니 links an observed first state to a later change. For the result of your own action, use -았/었더니 instead.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 직접 보고 느낀 내용을 말할 때 어떤 표현이 자연스러워요?
처음 상태와 나중 상태를 이어 말할 때 어떤 표현이 좋아요?
내 행동 때문에 생긴 결과에는 어떤 형태를 써야 해요?

culturalNote.title: Korean marks how you know
culturalNote.body: A Korean review often hints at the evidence source. -더라고요 tells the listener this came from your own experience, not just a rumor or general fact.
culturalNote.tip: Before using -더라고요, ask: did I personally see, hear, feel, try, or realize this?

inlineExercises.prompt: You visited the restaurant yourself and noticed it was crowded. Which sentence fits best?
Which sentence shows an observed change over time?
inlineExercises.explanation: -더니 connects the observed first state with the later change.

inlineExercises.prompt: You ate a lot, so you became sleepy. Which form is correct?
inlineExercises.explanation: Use -았/었더니 for your own action leading to a result.

bullets: -더라고요 reports what you personally noticed or realized.
-더니 connects an observed earlier state/action with a later change.
가 보니까, 생각보다, 처음에는, 예전에는, and 요즘은 make the observation scene clearer.
Use -았/었더니, not plain -더니, for your own action causing a result.
